summary: A reply to a complaint in RFC 531 that the UCSB resource evaluators had not read the Resource Notebook before testing services. The author argues there was a misunderstanding about what the evaluators were trying to do and how that differs from the aims of the software repository idea.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC responds to criticism of the UCSB resource evaluators. It explains what documentation they consult and what else they examine when evaluating a service.

subtitle: UCSB's response to criticism of its resource evaluations.

tldr.problem: RFC 531 criticized UCSB evaluators for not consulting the Resource Notebook and raised a question about their goals.
tldr.mechanism: John Pickens describes their documentation process and explains that evaluations also examined system behavior and usability.
tldr.outcome: The reply clarifies the evaluators' approach and says they make suggestions for improvement.

sections.title: Replying to the Criticism
sections.content:
John Pickens responds to comments in RFC 531 about UCSB resource evaluators and their use of the Resource Notebook. He says there is a misunderstanding about the evaluators' goals and notes that other people, not only the evaluators, were using the network.

He also says the OLS TELNET did not echo lowercase characters, which could confuse users during login.
sections.plainLanguage: Pickens says the criticism reflects a misunderstanding of the evaluators' work. He also points to a TELNET behavior that could make login confusing.

sections.title: The Evaluation Process
sections.content:
Pickens says UCSB evaluators begin by reading the Resource Notebook. If it does not answer their questions, they consult online documentation at the NIC and then at the site being evaluated; only after that do they contact a consultant.

Consultation might be online or by telephone and could include buying user manuals. Pickens says they prefer public documentation before contacting a technical liaison.
sections.plainLanguage: The evaluators start with the Resource Notebook, then check online documentation at the NIC and the site. They contact a person if questions remain.

sections.title: What Evaluators Examine
sections.content:
The author says resource evaluators examine more than documentation. Their work includes help facilities, online consultation, response time, reliability, and human engineering, and they make suggestions for improvement.

Pickens says they are learning how to make their reports constructive and apologizes to anyone they may have offended.
sections.plainLanguage: Evaluators test how a service behaves and how it supports users, not just what its documents say. Pickens says they aim to make their feedback constructive.

references.text: Padlipsky, M. A., "Feast of Famine", RFC 531, July 1973.
